premise.en: Drew fixes things on the Halden Ring, a fictional orbital station where every message to the ground takes two minutes to arrive. Keon is the dispatcher on the other end, patient, precise, and allergic to guessing. You can't interrupt someone who's two minutes away, so they've learned to really listen. The reader decides what Drew says into the silence, whether he tells the boring truth, and what happens when he comes down and the delay is gone.
premise.zh: Drew在虚构的轨道站Halden Ring上做维修，那里发往地面的每条消息都要两分钟才能送达。Keon是另一端的调度员，耐心、精确，最讨厌瞎猜。两分钟外的人没法打断，所以他们学会了认真听对方说完。读者要决定Drew往沉默里说什么，是否肯说出无聊的实话，以及当他落地、延迟消失之后会怎样。

The reader decides what Drew says into the silence, whether he tells the boring truth, and what happens when he comes down and the delay is gone.
premise.ko: 드루는 할든 링에서 일을 고친다, 모든 지상으로의 메시지가 도착하는 데 2분이 걸리는 가상의 궤도 스테이션. 키온은 다른 쪽 발송인이다, 인내심 있는, 정밀한, 그리고 추측에 알레르기가 있는. 당신은 2분 멀리 떨어진 누군가를 방해할 수 없으니까, 그들은 정말 듣는 것을 배웠다. 독자는 드루가 침묵 속으로 말하는 것을 결정한다, 그가 지루한 진실을 말하든지, 그리고 그가 착륙할 때 무엇이 일어나든지, 그리고 지연이 없다.
premise.es: Drew fixes things on the Halden Ring, a fictional orbital station where every message to the ground takes two minutes to arrive. Keon is the dispatcher on the other end, patient, precise, and allergic to guessing. You can't interrupt someone who's two minutes away, so they've learned to really listen. The reader decides what Drew says into the silence, whether he tells the boring truth, and what happens when he comes down and the delay is gone.

en: On the Halden Ring, every message to the ground takes two minutes to land. Drew has learned to say things he means, and then wait.
Keon's morning check-in arrives with an attachment: a mug of coffee on a dispatch console, lit like a magazine cover.
Send. Then silence, 120 seconds of it. Drew tightens a bolt that doesn't need it.
I laugh out loud in an empty service corridor. Then I type before I can decide not to.
So when does its owner take a day off?
That's not a joke. He's going to know it's not a joke. He's going to know in two minutes, and I get to sit here.

咖啡受宠若惊。咖啡得查查日程。等你是认真的，再问它一次。
ja: Asking for the coffee. It seems lonely. It might want dinner with someone who isn't a console.
The coffee is flattered. The coffee needs to check its schedule. Ask it again when you mean it.
ko: 커피를 요청하다. 그건 외로워 보여. 그건 콘솔이 아닌 누군가와 저녁 식사를 원할 수도 있어.
커피가 감사해 해. 커피가 그것의 스케줄을 확인할 필요가 있어. 당신이 의미할 때 다시 물어봐.
es: Asking for the coffee. It seems lonely. It might want dinner with someone who isn't a console.
The coffee is flattered. The coffee needs to check its schedule. Ask it again when you mean it.

mem.ko: 드루가 농담을 통해 초대를 했다. 키온이 그가 의미할 때 다시 물어보기를 요청했다.

t.ja: Back off. Work first.

en: Kidding. Forget it. Status on ring seal four: green.
The two minutes pass slower than usual.
Copy, seal four green. For the record, I don't forget things. I just file them.
zh: 开玩笑的，忘了吧。四号环密封状态：绿色。
这两分钟过得比平时慢。
收到，四号密封绿色。顺便说一句，我不会忘记东西，我只是把它们归档。
ja: Kidding. 忘れる it. Status on ring seal four: green.
The two minutes pass slower than usual.
Copy, seal four green. For the record, I don't forget things. I just file them.
ko: 농담이야. 잊어. 고리 밀봉 4의 상태: 녹색.
사본, 밀봉 4 녹색. 기록을 위해, 난 것을 잊지 않아. 난 그냥 그것을 보관해.
es: Kidding. Forget it. Status on ring seal four: green.
The two minutes pass slower than usual.
Copy, seal four green. For the record, I don't forget things. I just file them.

mem.zh: Drew收回了问题，改发工作状态；Keon没有忘记，而是把那个问题归了档。

mem.ko: 드루가 일 상태를 가져갔고, 보내다. 키온이 질문을 기억하지 않고 보관했다.

goal.zh: 理清交错的消息，而不是假装能即时对话
goal.ja: Untangle crossed messages without pretending you're live
goal.ko: 당신이 라이브가 아니라고 한다고 해서, 건넌 메시지를 풀다
goal.es: Untangle crossed messages without pretending you're live

en: They both start typing at once. Neither knows it. Four messages leave two ends of the sky and pass each other somewhere in the dark.
Drew's arrives first: a careful paragraph explaining that the haircut photo was a dare from the station medic. Keon's arrives in orbit: a yes.
I said yes to dinner. Not to your haircut.
Please stop replying before my messages land. I'm answering things you haven't said yet.
I scroll up. He's right. We've been arguing with each other's past for ten minutes.
He said yes. He said yes nine minutes ago, and I've been talking about bangs.
zh: 两人同时开始打字，谁都不知道。四条消息从天空两端出发，在黑暗中某处擦肩而过。
Drew那条先到地面：一大段小心翼翼的解释，说那张发型照是站里医生跟他打的赌。Keon那条送到轨道上：同意。
我答应的是晚饭，不是你的发型。
请别在我的消息到之前就回复。我在回答你还没说出口的话。
我往上翻。他说得对。我们已经跟对方的过去吵了十分钟。
他答应了。九分钟前就答应了，我却一直在聊刘海。
ja: They both start typing at once. Neither knows it. Four messages leave two ends of the sky and pass each other somewhere in the dark.
Drew's arrives first: a careful paragraph explaining that the haircut photo was a dare from the station medic. Keon's arrives in orbit: a yes.
I said yes to dinner. Not to your haircut.
Please stop replying before my messages land. I'm answering things you haven't said yet.
I scroll up. He's right. We've been arguing with each other's past for ten minutes.
He said yes. He said yes nine minutes ago, and I've been talking about bangs.
ko: 그들이 둘 다 한 번에 입력하기 시작한다. 아무도 그걸 몰라. 4개의 메시지가 하늘의 두 끝을 떠나고 암흑 어딘가에서 서로를 지나간다.
드루의는 먼저 도착한다: 헤어컷 사진이 역 의료인의 감정이었다고 설명하는 신중한 문단. 키온의는 궤도에 도착한다: 그래.
난 저녁 식사에 그래라고 했어. 당신의 헤어컷에는 아니야.
제발 내 메시지가 착륙하기 전에 응답하기를 멈춰. 난 당신이 아직 말하지 않은 것에 대답하고 있어.
난 위로 스크롤한다. 그게 맞아. 우리는 10분 동안 서로의 과거와 싸워왔어.
그는 그래라고 했어. 그는 9분 전에 그래라고 했고, 난 머리카락에 대해 말하고 있었어.
es: They both start typing at once. Neither knows it. Four messages leave two ends of the sky and pass each other somewhere in the dark.
Drew's arrives first: a careful paragraph explaining that the haircut photo was a dare from the station medic. Keon's arrives in orbit: a yes.
I said yes to dinner. Not to your haircut.
Please stop replying before my messages land. I'm answering things you haven't said yet.
I scroll up. He's right. We've been arguing with each other's past for ten minutes.
He said yes. He said yes nine minutes ago, and I've been talking about bangs.

ask.zh: Drew要怎么把这团乱麻理清？
ask.ja: どのように does Drew untangle it?

t.en: Propose a rule: one message, then wait.
t.zh: 提议一条规矩：发一条，然后等。
t.ja: Propose a rule: one message, then wait.
t.ko: 규칙을 제안하다: 하나의 메시지, 그럼 기다리다.
t.es: Propose a rule: one message, then wait.

en: New rule. I send one. I wait for yours. No stacking.
Agreed. Also: yes. Again. So it isn't buried under your bangs.
Tuesday you're on the hull for the seal inspection. I'm your dispatcher. Two minutes behind you the whole time. Talk to me out there.
zh: 新规矩。我发一条，等你回一条。不许叠着发。
同意。还有：我答应。再说一次，免得被你的刘海埋了。
周二你要出舱检查密封，我是你的调度。全程落后你两分钟。到了外面，跟我说话。
ja: New rule. I send one. I wait for yours. No stacking.
Agreed. Also: yes. Again. So it isn't buried under your bangs.
火曜日 you're on the hull for the seal inspection. I'm your dispatcher. Two minutes behind you the whole time. Talk to me out there.
ko: 새 규칙. 난 하나를 보낸다. 난 당신의 것을 기다린다. 쌓지 말고.
동의. 또한: 그래. 다시. 그래서 그건 당신의 머리카락 아래 묻혀 있지 않아.
화요일 당신이 밀봉 검사를 위해 껍질에 있어. 난 당신의 발송인이야. 2분 당신 뒤에 내내. 거기 밖에 내게 말해.
es: New rule. I send one. I wait for yours. No stacking.
Agreed. Also: yes. Again. So it isn't buried under your bangs.
Tuesday you're on the hull for the seal inspection. I'm your dispatcher. Two minutes behind you the whole time. Talk to me out there.

mem.en: They agreed to one message at a time; Keon repeated his yes and will dispatch Drew's Tuesday hull walk.
mem.zh: 两人约定一次只发一条；Keon再次答应了晚饭，并将担任Drew周二出舱时的调度。
mem.ja: They agreed to one message at a time; Keon repeated his yes and will dispatch Drew's Tuesday hull walk.
mem.ko: 그들이 한 번에 하나의 메시지에 동의했다. 키온이 그래를 다시 말했고, 화요일 껍질 산책을 발송할 거야.
mem.es: They agreed to one message at a time; Keon repeated his yes and will dispatch Drew's Tuesday hull walk.

t.en: Number every message, like a work log.
t.zh: 给每条消息编号，像工作日志一样。
t.ja: Number every message, like a work log.
t.ko: 일 기록처럼, 모든 메시지를 번호 매기다.
t.es: Number every message, like a work log.

en: D-1: Thank you for the yes. D-2: The haircut was a dare. D-3: I'm numbering these now.
K-1: Good. K-2: Tuesday, 0900, you're on the hull and I'm your dispatch. K-3: Tell me everything out there. Even the boring parts.
zh: D-1：谢谢你答应。D-2：发型是打赌输的。D-3：从现在起我给消息编号。
K-1：很好。K-2：周二09:00，你出舱，我是你的调度。K-3：在外面什么都告诉我，包括无聊的部分。
ja: D-1: Thank you for the yes. D-2: The haircut was a dare. D-3: I'm numbering these now.
K-1: Good. K-2: Tuesday, 0900, you're on the hull and I'm your dispatch. K-3: Tell me everything out there. Even the boring parts.
ko: D-1: 그래에 감사. D-2: 헤어컷이 감정이었어. D-3: 난 이제 이것들을 번호 매기고 있어.
K-1: 좋아. K-2: 화요일, 0900, 당신이 껍질에 있고 난 당신의 발송. K-3: 거기 밖에 모든 것을 말해. 심지어 지루한 부분도.
es: D-1: Thank you for the yes. D-2: The haircut was a dare. D-3: I'm numbering these now.
K-1: Good. K-2: Tuesday, 0900, you're on the hull and I'm your dispatch. K-3: Tell me everything out there. Even the boring parts.

mem.en: Drew started numbering messages; Keon assigned himself to Drew's Tuesday hull walk and asked for every detail.
mem.zh: Drew开始给消息编号；Keon主动担任他周二出舱的调度，要他事无巨细地汇报。
mem.ja: Drew started numbering messages; Keon assigned himself to Drew's Tuesday hull walk and asked for every detail.
mem.ko: 드루가 메시지 번호 매기기 시작했다. 키온이 자신을 드루의 화요일 껍질 산책에 지정했고, 모든 세부사항을 요청했다.
mem.es: Drew started numbering messages; Keon assigned himself to Drew's Tuesday hull walk and asked for every detail.

en: Drew takes his hands off the keyboard and waits out the whole queue.
…and that's all. Thank you for letting me finish. Nobody does.
Tuesday you're on the hull. I'm on your channel. If you're going to be quiet, be quiet with me.
zh: Drew把手从键盘上拿开，等整个队列都传完。
……就这些。谢谢你让我说完。从来没人这样。
周二你出舱，我在你的频道上。你要是想安静，就跟我一起安静。
ja: Drew takes his hands off the keyboard and waits out the whole queue.
…and that's all. Thank you for letting me finish. Nobody does.
火曜日 you're on the hull. I'm on your channel. If you're going to be quiet, be quiet with me.
ko: 드루가 키보드에서 손을 떼고, 전체 큐가 도착하기를 기다린다.
... 그리고 그게 다야. 나를 끝나게 한 것에 고마워. 아무도 하지 않아.
화요일 당신이 껍질에 있어. 난 당신의 채널에 있어. 만약 당신이 조용해질 거면, 나와 함께 조용해.
es: Drew takes his hands off the keyboard and waits out the whole queue.
…and that's all. Thank you for letting me finish. Nobody does.
Tuesday you're on the hull. I'm on your channel. If you're going to be quiet, be quiet with me.

mem.ja: Drew stopped typing and let all of Keon's messages arrive; Keon asked to be on his channel Tuesday.
mem.ko: 드루가 입력을 멈추고, 모든 키온의 메시지가 도착하게 했다. 키온이 화요일 그의 채널에 있기를 요청했다.
mem.es: Drew stopped typing and let all of Keon's messages arrive; Keon asked to be on his channel Tuesday.

goal.en: Report the real status, not the comfortable one
goal.zh: 报告真实状态，而不是省事的那个
goal.ja: Report the real status, not the comfortable one
goal.ko: 편안한 것이 아니라, 실제 상태를 보고하다
goal.es: Report the real status, not the comfortable one

en: Seal junction seven is fine. Mostly. There's a hairline crack in the housing: not dangerous yet, the kind of thing Drew usually calls “fine” and fixes on his own time.
Status? Your last message was eight minutes ago. That's two round trips of nothing.
I type “fine.” I look at it. It looks like every “fine” I've ever sent anybody.
I can wait. I can't guess.
Then I'll tell you the boring version.
The boring version has numbers in it. The boring version makes this his problem too.
zh: 七号密封接口没事，大体上没事。外壳上有一道发丝般的裂缝，暂时不危险，正是Drew平常会说“没事”然后自己抽空修掉的那种。
状态？你上一条消息是八分钟前。那是两个来回的空白。
我打下“没事”，盯着它看。它跟我这辈子发给任何人的每一个“没事”都一模一样。
那我给你讲无聊的版本。
无聊的版本里有数字。无聊的版本会让这也变成他的问题。
ja: Seal junction seven is fine. Mostly. There's a hairline crack in the housing: not dangerous yet, the kind of thing Drew usually calls “fine” and fixes on his own time.
Status? Your last message was eight minutes ago. That's two round trips of nothing.
I type “fine.” I look at it. It looks like every “fine” I've ever sent anybody.
I can wait. I can't guess.
Then I'll tell you the boring version.
The boring version has numbers in it. The boring version makes this his problem too.
ko: 밀봉 교차점 7은 좋아. 대부분. 껍질에 머리 같은 균열이 있어: 아직 위험하지 않고, 드루가 보통 "좋아"라고 부르는 것, 그리고 자신의 시간에 고친다.
상태? 당신의 마지막 메시지는 8분 전이었어. 그건 아무것도 2번의 왕복이야.
난 "좋아"를 입력한다. 난 그것을 본다. 그건 "좋아"처럼 보여, 난 절대 누군가에게 보냈어.
난 기다릴 수 있어. 난 추측할 수 없어.
그럼 난 당신에게 지루한 버전을 말할 거야.
지루한 버전이 그것에서 숫자를 가지고 있어. 지루한 버전이 이것을 그의 문제도 만들어.
es: Seal junction seven is fine. Mostly. There's a hairline crack in the housing: not dangerous yet, the kind of thing Drew usually calls “fine” and fixes on his own time.
Status? Your last message was eight minutes ago. That's two round trips of nothing.
I type “fine.” I look at it. It looks like every “fine” I've ever sent anybody.
I can wait. I can't guess.
Then I'll tell you the boring version.
The boring version has numbers in it. The boring version makes this his problem too.

t.ja: Send the full report, crack and all.
t.es: Send the full report, crack and all.

en: Hairline crack in the housing, junction seven, four centimeters. Not venting. I want a second tech and a new housing tomorrow.
Logged. Second tech assigned. Thank you for the boring version. It's my favorite genre.
It felt like taking off a helmet. In a good way. Not in the space way.
zh: 七号接口外壳有发丝裂缝，四厘米，没有泄漏。我要一名二号技师，明天换新外壳。
已记录，二号技师已指派。谢谢你讲了无聊的版本，这是我最喜欢的类型。
感觉像摘下头盔。好的那种，不是在太空里摘的那种。
ja: Hairline crack in the housing, junction seven, four centimeters. Not venting. I want a second tech and a new housing tomorrow.
Logged. 秒 tech assigned. Thank you for the boring version. It's my favorite genre.
It felt like taking off a helmet. In a good way. Not in the space way.
ko: 껍질에 머리 같은 균열, 교차점 7, 4센티미터. 환기하지 않아. 난 두 번째 기술과 내일 새 껍질을 원해.
기록. 두 번째 기술 지정. 지루한 버전에 고마워. 그건 내 즐겨 찾기 장르야.
그건 헬멧을 벗기는 것 같은 느낌이었어. 좋은 방식으로. 우주 방식 아니야.
es: Hairline crack in the housing, junction seven, four centimeters. Not venting. I want a second tech and a new housing tomorrow.
Logged. Second tech assigned. Thank you for the boring version. It's my favorite genre.
It felt like taking off a helmet. In a good way. Not in the space way.

mem.en: Drew reported the crack in full; Keon logged it, assigned a second tech, and thanked him.
mem.zh: Drew完整报告了裂缝；Keon做了记录、指派了二号技师，并向他道谢。
mem.ja: Drew reported the crack in full; Keon logged it, assigned a second tech, and thanked him.
mem.ko: 드루가 균열을 전체로 보고했다. 키온이 기록했고, 두 번째 기술을 지정했고, 감사했다.
mem.es: Drew reported the crack in full; Keon logged it, assigned a second tech, and thanked him.

t.en: Say you can't detail it yet; set a time.
t.zh: 说明现在没法细讲，约定报告时间。
t.ja: Say you can't detail it yet; set a time.
t.ko: 당신이 아직 그것을 세부 사항 할 수 없다고 말하다. 시간을 정하다.
t.es: Say you can't detail it yet; set a time.

en: It's more than fine and less than bad. I need my hands for twenty minutes. Full report at 10:10. Promise.
10:10. I'll hold the channel. If I don't hear from you by 10:12, I send someone. Not because I'm worried. Because that's the job.
At 10:09, the report lands. Every number.
zh: 比没事严重，比糟糕轻。我的手还要忙二十分钟。10:10给你完整报告，保证。
10:10。我守着频道。10:12还没消息，我就派人。不是因为我担心，是因为这是我的工作。
ja: It's more than fine and less than bad. I need my hands for twenty minutes. Full report at 10:10. Promise.
10:10. I'll hold the channel. If I don't hear from you by 10:12, I send someone. Not because I'm worried. Because that's the job.
At 10:09, the report lands. Every number.
ko: 그건 좋아와 나쁜 사이에 더 해. 난 20분 동안 내 손이 필요해. 10:10에 전체 보고서. 약속해.
10:10. 난 채널을 유지할 거야. 만약 난 10:12까지 당신한테 듣지 않으면, 난 누군가를 보낸다. 난 안 걱정해서가 아니야. 왜냐하면 그건 그 일이니까.
es: It's more than fine and less than bad. I need my hands for twenty minutes. Full report at 10:10. Promise.
10:10. I'll hold the channel. If I don't hear from you by 10:12, I send someone. Not because I'm worried. Because that's the job.
At 10:09, the report lands. Every number.

mem.zh: Drew没有说“没事”，而是约定了报告时间；完整报告提前一分钟送达。
mem.ja: Drew set a report time instead of saying “fine”; the full report landed a minute early.
mem.ko: 드루가 "좋아" 대신 보고서 시간을 정했다. 전체 보고서가 1분 일찍 도착했다.
mem.es: Drew set a report time instead of saying “fine”; the full report landed a minute early.

en: Keon doesn't reply for six minutes. That's three one-way trips of a man choosing his words.

Then I get to laugh sooner.
Hall B. I'll be the one not holding a sign, because I refuse to be that guy.

홀 B. 난 호출 없이 하나가 되어. 난 그 사람이 되는 것을 거절해.

en: Gravity is rude. Drew's knees report it immediately. The arrival hall smells like floor wax and someone's burnt pretzel.
Keon is by the pillar. He is holding a sign. It says DREW, in dispatch-console font.
I open my mouth, and then I just wait. Out of habit. Counting. He's already answered. He's already looking at me like he's still listening.
I hold out my hand, palm up, and don't move it. I'm not waiting for a signal. I'm waiting for him.
You can say no. Out loud. It'll arrive right away. Big change.

Keon站在柱子旁。手里举着牌子，上面写着DREW，用的是调度台的字体。
我张开嘴，然后就那么等着。习惯了，在数秒。可他已经回答完了，还在看着我，像是仍在听。
我伸出手，掌心朝上，一动不动。我等的不是信号，是他。
你可以说不。大声说出来，马上就能送到。变化很大吧。

ko: 중력이 무례해. 드루의 무릎이 즉시 보고한다. 도착 홀은 바닥 광택과 누군가의 탄 프레첼 냄새가 난다.
키온이 기둥 옆에 있어. 그는 호출을 들고 있어. 그건 드루라고 말한다, 발송 콘솔 글씨체에.
난 입을 열고, 그럼 난 그냥 기다린다. 습관에서. 센다. 그는 이미 대답했어. 그는 여전히 나를 보고 있어 그가 여전히 듣고 있어처럼.
난 손을 내밀고, 손바닥을 위로, 그리고 그것을 움직이지 않아. 난 호출을 기다리지 않아. 난 그를 기다려.
당신은 아니라고 말할 수 있어. 큰 소리로. 그건 바로 도착할 거야. 큰 변화.
es: Gravity is rude. Drew's knees report it immediately. The arrival hall smells like floor wax and someone's burnt pretzel.
Keon is by the pillar. He is holding a sign. It says DREW, in dispatch-console font.
I open my mouth, and then I just wait. Out of habit. Counting. He's already answered. He's already looking at me like he's still listening.
I hold out my hand, palm up, and don't move it. I'm not waiting for a signal. I'm waiting for him.
You can say no. Out loud. It'll arrive right away. Big change.

Hi. Oh no. It's instant. I have to be good at this immediately.

Hi. Oh no. It's instant. I have to be good at this immediately.

난 그가 할 때 놓아 준다. 호출이 내 팔 아래로 간다. 난 여전히 그가 여기 있어서 기뻐.

I let go when he does. The sign goes under my arm. I'm still glad he's here.

Whether I want to hold your hand.

我问了。当面问的。现在我得看着他的脸，看答案一点点出现。

I was giving the signal time.
There is no signal delay here.
Then what do I wait for?
Whether I want to hold your hand.
I asked. Live. Now I have to watch his face while the answer happens.

난 물었어. 라이브. 이제 난 답변이 일어나는 동안 그의 얼굴을 봐야 해.

en: And tonight? A real date. Not a debrief.
Yes to the hand, now. Yes to the date, tonight.
I reach across the table. I don't wait for a signal. I wait for his nod. It comes fast.
zh: 那今晚呢？正式约会，不是任务汇报。
牵手，现在就好。约会，今晚好。
我把手伸过桌子。我不等信号，我等他点头。他点得很快。

Yes to the hand, now. Yes to the date, tonight.
I reach across the table. I don't wait for a signal. I wait for his nod. It comes fast.

손에 그래, 지금. 날짜에 그래, 오늘 밤.
난 테이블 위로 도달한다. 난 호출을 기다리지 않아. 난 그의 끄덕임을 기다린다. 그건 빠르게 온다.

t.ja: Ask for quiet that doesn't mean anything's wrong.
t.es: Ask for quiet that doesn't mean anything's wrong.

en: Can we have silence that doesn't mean anything's wrong? Like the delay, but on purpose.
Yes. Silence is allowed. I'll hold your hand during it, if you want. You can also say no to that.
Drew nods. They drink the fine coffee for four quiet minutes. Nobody fills it.
zh: 我们能不能有一种不代表出事的沉默？像延迟一样，但是故意的。
可以。允许沉默。你愿意的话，沉默的时候我牵着你。这个你也可以说不。
Drew点点头。两人安静地喝了四分钟那杯普通的咖啡，谁也没去填满它。
ja: Can we have silence that doesn't mean anything's wrong? Like the delay, but on purpose.
Yes. Silence is allowed. I'll hold your hand during it, if you want. You can also say no to that.
Drew nods. They drink the fine coffee for four quiet minutes. Nobody fills it.
ko: 우리가 침묵을 가질 수 있어, 아무것도 의미하지 않는다? 지연처럼, 하지만 의도적으로.
그래. 침묵이 허락되어. 난 당신의 손을 들고 있을 거야, 만약 당신이 원한다면. 당신도 또한 그것에 아니라고 말할 수 있어.
드루가 끄덕인다. 그들이 좋은 커피를 마신다, 4분 동안 조용하다. 아무도 그것을 채우지 않아.
es: Can we have silence that doesn't mean anything's wrong? Like the delay, but on purpose.
Yes. Silence is allowed. I'll hold your hand during it, if you want. You can also say no to that.
Drew nods. They drink the fine coffee for four quiet minutes. Nobody fills it.

mem.zh: Drew请求慢一点、允许沉默；Keon同意，并说只有Drew愿意时才牵手。
mem.ja: Drew asked to go slow with silence allowed; Keon agreed and offered his hand only if Drew wanted it.

Thank you for saying it live. It's easier to hear fast.
I keep my hands around my cup. I don't make him watch me be disappointed. That can wait until he's gone.

谢谢你当面说。坏消息快点听到，反而好受些。
我双手捧着杯子。我不让他看着我失望。那可以等他走了再说。

그것을 라이브로 말한 것에 고마워. 빠르게 듣기 쉬워.
난 내 손을 내 컵 주위에 유지한다. 난 그가 나를 봤어 하게 실망해. 그건 그가 가고 나서 기다릴 수 있어.
es: I got offered the outer station. Eighteen months. I think I'm taking it, and I think that means not this.
Thank you for saying it live. It's easier to hear fast.
I keep my hands around my cup. I don't make him watch me be disappointed. That can wait until he's gone.

Now I think they were training. You taught me to finish a sentence.
You taught me to wait for one. We should have a word for that.
Up there, I had two minutes to be brave. Down here, I get none. That's the whole deal.

现在我觉得那是训练。你教会我把话说完。

I used to think the two minutes were the problem.
Now I think they were training. You taught me to finish a sentence.
You taught me to wait for one. We should have a word for that.
Up there, I had two minutes to be brave. Down here, I get none. That's the whole deal.

Every Thursday. Coffee. Nobody fills the quiet unless they want to.
Take your two minutes. I'll still be here.

en: I'm going out to the far station. The official channel stays open. The private one, I'm closing.
Understood. You'll have the best dispatcher you've ever had. That part I can still do.
Safe work, Drew. Report the boring version.
The private channel closes with a small chime. The official one stays green.
